name: Homotaurine (tramiprosate)
short: Tramiprosate, 24 people with amyloid angiopathy and past brain bleeds, all treated: 9 bled again, all in advanced disease, no apparent dose link. Alzheimer's trial, 1,052: adverse events like placebo.
text: Most safety data come from trials of homotaurine as the investigational drug tramiprosate, taken by mouth, in people with Alzheimer's disease. In a 78-week placebo-controlled trial in 1,052 patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease, the incidence of adverse events was similar across treatment groups; a re-analysis of two 78-week placebo-controlled phase 3 trials (2,025 patients) described tramiprosate safety as favourable in patients homozygous for the APOE4 allele (about 13-15% of participants) and named nausea, vomiting, depression and decreased weight as the most common adverse events; the abstract does not make clear whether this list covers all 2,025 patients or only that subgroup. In a phase II trial in 58 patients, the most frequent side effects were nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea, intermittent and mild to moderate, with no tramiprosate-related serious adverse events; seven treated participants stopped because of side effects. In a phase 2 trial in 24 people with cerebral amyloid angiopathy and previous brain bleeds, all randomised to one of three doses of tramiprosate by mouth for 12 weeks (the abstract describes no placebo group), nausea and vomiting were the most common adverse events and were more frequent at high doses; nine participants had new brain haemorrhages during treatment, all in those with advanced disease and with no apparent link to dose. A small randomised study of homotaurine in Parkinson's disease with cognitive impairment reported mild gastrointestinal side effects in 3 patients. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
